subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: For LiteLLM/Vertex beta generic 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, should OpenClaw classify it as recoverable provider/session state, and which recovery should run before surfacing a message?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but broad recovery semantics can change provider fallback/session behavior and misclassify unrelated invalid request errors without maintainer intent and live provider proof.

options.title: Narrow provider-owned classification
options.body: Add a LiteLLM/Vertex hook for the proven response shape, emit actionable copy, and avoid a broad generic `INVALID_ARGUMENT` catch.

options.title: Wait for live proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open without code until a maintainer or reporter captures the exact LiteLLM/Vertex error object and lane state in a real run.

options.title: Broader session circuit breaker
options.body: Handle repeated 400 invalid-argument loops after a bounded failure count with compaction, pruning, fallback, or session cleanup if maintainers accept broader semantics.

recommendation.title: Narrow provider-owned classification
recommendation.body: Add a LiteLLM/Vertex hook for the proven response shape, emit actionable copy, and avoid a broad generic `INVALID_ARGUMENT` catch.
